salient_findings: 1-year history of slow but progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft
4 × 4 cm area of swelling with mild blanching erythema
No fluid or purulence obtained on percutaneous aspiration
Complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass excised from subcutaneous tissue
key_facts: 32-year-old woman presented with a 1-year history of swelling
Swelling located near the gluteal cleft
Patient denied fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
No fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
Percutaneous aspiration was performed but no fluid was obtained
Differential diagnosis included inclusion cyst and soft-tissue tumor
Surgical excision was performed
A 6-cm vertical incision was made over the lesion
The mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the description of a complex and septated mass in the subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: similar to epidermoid cyst, could be considered given the location and characteristics of the mass

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the description of the mass being adherent to subcutaneous fat

shortlist.label: Angiolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: could be considered given the location and characteristics of the mass, although less common

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: possible diagnosis given the description of a solid, multiloculated mass in the subcutaneous tissue

raw.rationale: The patient presented with a slow-growing, progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft, which is consistent with an epidermoid cyst. The absence of fluid or purulence on aspiration and the presence of a solid, multiloculated mass on surgical excision also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: While dermoid cysts can also present as slow-growing masses, they often contain hair, teeth, or other tissue, which was not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically soft, mobile, and not adherent to surrounding tissue, which does not match the description of the mass in this case.

rejected.label: Angiolipoma
rejected.why: Angiolipomas are a type of lipoma that contains blood vessels, but they are not typically described as complex and septated masses.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: Desmoid tumors are aggressive, infiltrative tumors that can cause significant symptoms, which does not match the patient's presentation of a slow-growing, asymptomatic mass.
